title: String Quartet in B-flat major, Op. 76 No. 4, “Sunrise”
hook: A violin melody climbs slowly out of a held chord, like the sun over the horizon.

painting.title: Sunrise in the Catskills
painting.pairingNote: The first light spreads slowly over a mountain valley, as the violin’s tune rises over the still, held chord that gave the quartet its name.

facts: Haydn wrote the quartet in 1797, aged 65, after his second stay in London. It is the fourth of six quartets for the Hungarian Count Joseph Erdődy, published in 1799 as Op. 76; the third is the “Emperor”.
The name “Sunrise” is not Haydn’s. It comes from the opening: the three lower instruments hold a quiet chord while the first violin’s melody rises slowly above it.

In the same year Haydn was at work on his oratorio *The Creation*, whose most famous moment is a sudden blaze of light. Some listeners hear the quartet’s opening as a gentler sunrise of the same kind.
In Germany it was once also called the “Tannhäuser” quartet, because its opening tune reminded listeners of a march in Wagner’s opera, written half a century later.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a slow sunrise and bright, busy music in turn (I), a searching, meditative Adagio (II), a sturdy minuet with a bagpipe-like trio (III), a cosy country tune that ends in a whirlwind (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro con spirito
movements.summary: The movement is built on a contrast between two kinds of sound. In one, three instruments hold a soft chord and a single line rises slowly above it; in the other, all four play quick, lively figures together. The two take turns all through this [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement.

mainIdeas.name: The sunrise
mainIdeas.description: a long, rising melody in the first violin over a soft chord held by the other three. Later the long line moves down into the cello, winding downwards, with the violins and viola holding the chord above it.

mainIdeas.name: The busy music
mainIdeas.description: quick runs and short, detached notes, tossed between the four players, loud and bright.

stops.hear: Very quiet: a chord held by three instruments, and the first violin rising slowly above it
Suddenly loud and busy: quick runs pass from player to player
Quiet again: now the long line is deep in the cello, winding downwards under a held chord
stops.happening: The sunrise idea, turned upside down

stops.hear: The quiet opening again
The held chord returns, but darker, in a minor key; the violin rises over it
The music grows quieter and quieter
stops.happening: The way back to the home key

stops.hear: The violin rises over the held chord in the home key
The rising line climbs up from the cello, through the viola, to the second violin
stops.happening: The theme passed upwards through the quartet

stops.hear: A held pause; then each of the upper three in turn plays a scrap of the sunrise

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: All four play loud, firm chords
stops.happening: The movement closes in B-flat major

notice: Notice how slow the opening sounds, though the movement is marked Allegro. The held chord makes time seem to stand still; the busy music sets it moving again.

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.summary: A slow movement in E-flat major that sounds more like a meditation than a song. The theme starts hesitantly, a few notes at a time with pauses between, and is then led through unexpected harmonies. The movement falls into two halves that begin the same way, the second one darker.

mainIdeas.name: The hesitant theme
mainIdeas.description: three notes rocking around one pitch, then a held note with a pause, repeated a step higher.

mainIdeas.name: The ripples
mainIdeas.description: quick, decorative figures in the first violin.

mainIdeas.name: The clashes
mainIdeas.description: notes held over into the next chord, so the harmony grates for a moment before it resolves.

stops.hear: Very slow and quiet: a few notes, a pause, the same again a step higher
The same hesitant figure, now in a new key
The first violin breaks into quick, rippling figures
The opening figure again, with darker, more unexpected chords and longer pauses
Rippling figures again, reaching high
A low, loud trill, then the opening theme in the home key
Very soft; the first violin plays on its lower strings, and the harmony settles

notice: Listen to the pauses at the start. The theme seems to stop and listen to itself before going on.

movements.heading: Menuetto: Allegro
movements.summary: A brisk [[minuet|minuet]] built from a little two-note figure that rocks back and forth. At the end the music does not stop: one low note is held over into the [[trio|trio]], where a folk-like tune floats over a drone, like a bagpipe.

mainIdeas.name: The two-note figure
mainIdeas.description: a rocking pair of notes, repeated, then a leap up.

mainIdeas.name: The trio tune
mainIdeas.description: a simple, swaying melody in the first violin over long-held notes below.

stops.hear: Loud and lively: a little two-note figure rocks back and forth, then leaps up
The figure travels through other keys and between the instruments
stops.happening: The second half of the minuet, repeated

stops.hear: One note is held on and the music runs straight into a quiet, rustic tune over a long drone
The rocking figure returns

notice: Listen for the join between minuet and trio. Instead of a full stop and a fresh start, a single held note carries you across.

movements.heading: Finale: Allegro ma non troppo – Più allegro – Più presto
movements.tempo: Finale: Allegro ma non troppo – Più allegro – Più presto
movements.key: B-flat major – B-flat minor – B-flat major
movements.summary: The finale begins as an easy-going, cheerful tune, almost a country song. A middle section turns to the minor, with a few playful surprises. When the tune comes back it breaks off, and the quartet speeds up twice, ending in a whirl of fast notes.

mainIdeas.name: The tune
mainIdeas.description: a comfortable, singing melody in the first violin, in two short halves, each repeated.

mainIdeas.name: The minor episode
mainIdeas.description: the same kind of music in B-flat minor, more insistent.

mainIdeas.name: The whirlwind
mainIdeas.description: faster and then faster still, with the tune’s fragments spinning round.

stops.hear: Relaxed and smiling: the first violin sings a homely tune
stops.happening: The main tune, played softly (“mezza voce”)

stops.hear: The tune goes on and wanders a little
stops.happening: The second half of the tune, repeated

stops.hear: The mood darkens: louder, more insistent music in the minor
The homely tune returns in the major
The tune breaks off; the music jumps forward, faster
Faster still: all four race to the end

notice: Listen to how the tempo changes at the end. Haydn writes two separate speed-ups, so the last minute feels like a dance that gets out of hand.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: This was the second of the Takács Quartet’s Op. 76 albums for Decca, issued in 1989, with the founding leader Gábor Takács-Nagy as first violin.

threads.title: Held and moving
threads.body: The first movement sets long-held chords against busy music; the minuet’s held note leads into a trio over a drone; the finale lets go of all stillness at the end.

threads.title: Four voices
threads.body: The rising sunrise theme moves from the first violin to the cello and then up through the quartet. Listen for who has it.

threads.title: Light
threads.body: The opening’s slow rise, written while Haydn was working on *The Creation*, gave the quartet its name and colours how people have heard it ever since.
